2026 Roadmap

The 2026 competition will be conducted over 5-weeks, starting from the launch day (19 Sep 2026) and culminating in the pitch/ demo day (24 Oct 2026). The event tests your ability to plan and collaborate effectively across an extended duration.

Student teams will need to satisfy certain milestones to progress in the competition:

1. Attend the launch day and form your team on 19 Sep 2026 @ The University of Hong Kong, Pokfulam.

2. Report on your progress by 04 Oct 2026

3. Submit your pitch deck by 18 Oct 2026. Only 40 teams will be selected by the committee to progress to the final day. Finalists will be announced by 22 Oct 2026.

4. Deliver your pitch to a panel of judges on 24 Oct 2026 @ City University of Hong Kong @ Kowloon Tong.

2026 Master of Ceremonies - Mr. Michael Campion, Quinlan & Associates

Born and raised in Hong Kong, Michael Campion is a Partner and Head of Corporate Training at Quinlan & Associates. He has over a decade of experience performing on stage as a speaker and emcee, sharing the stage with CEOs and celebrities for corporate, educational and not-for-profits events. Michael has been interviewed by BBC World, SCMP, RTHK, and worked on live TV as a sports commentator. He also hosts the business and self-help podcast Playing The Inner Game.  Earlier in his career, Michael worked global banking and markets at Royal Bank of Scotland in Edinburgh and was a full-time professional football player in Hong Kong. He holds a Master of Business Management from the University of Edinburgh.

Launch Day Event

Date:  19 September 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 9:00 am – 4:00 pm
Venue: Lecture Hall II (Opposite Grand Hall Lee Shau Kee Lecture Centre), HKU Centennial Campus

What will students do:

  • Network with students across all eight public universities in Hong Kong
  • Learn about the event rules and prizes
  • Form a hackathon team
  • Brainstorm ideas and social issues
  • Hear from guest speakers around sustainable innovation, design thinking, and identifying your problems.
  • Receive free tokens from Tencent for the WorkBuddy AI platform

Indicative agenda

Morning Keynote Speakers

Professor Hayden So, Director of the School of Innovation, The University of Hong Kong

Keynote 1: Innovate with CARE

The advent of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is bringing rapid changes and drastic disruptions to all walks of life, and even more significant transformations are expected to come. This suggests that many existing norms are going to be modified and innovation is needed. But with GenAI starting to become even competent enough to solve mathematical challenges and the Millennium Prize Problems, how should we prepare ourselves to be innovators? Ensuring humans are in the centre of our considerations, this talk will suggest CARE as a framework of qualities for innovators in the current era.

About the speaker: Professor Hayden So is the Director and Associate Professor of the School of Innovation, the University of Hong Kong. Previously, he has been with the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering since 2007, where he served as the Co-director of the Computer Engineering program until 2024. His research is in the area of reconfigurable computing, hardware/software co-design, computer architecture, embedded systems and AI hardware. He is passionate about STEM education and believes in the transformative power of hands-on innovation projects on a person. His is a “triple bear” — having graduated from University of California, Berkeley three times with Ph.D., M.S., and B.S. degrees in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences. When not at work, he is usually traveling around the world looking for great coffee, great food, and great people.

Professor King Chow, Academic Registrar, Prof. Life Science, Chemical & Biological Engineering and Public Policy, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

Keynote 2: When the SDGs Become Obsolete, What Should We Do?

As the Sustainable Development Goals approach their 2030 horizon, they are unlikely to be fully achieved; yet this does not render them irrelevant. Rather, their underlying spirit must be renewed to address emerging gaps with greater precision. In a world reshaped by climate instability, geopolitical fragmentation, artificial intelligence, demographic shifts, and persistent inequality, we must move beyond a fixation on 17 goals and countable indicators. The next global framework should reaffirm the ethical core of sustainable development: human dignity, shared stewardship, equity, peace, and partnership. Future initiatives must be locally adaptive, technologically aware, and accountable to both material needs and humanistic aspirations. In this sense, obsolescence should become a mandate for renewal, redesign, and deeper global cooperation.
About the speaker: Professor King L. Chow is Academic Registrar and Professor of Life Science, Chemical and Biological Engineering, and Public Policy at HKUST. He previously led the Interdisciplinary Programs Office and the Dean of Students Office, overseeing academic, innovation, and student development initiatives. His research spans genetics, development, evolution, and synthetic biology, alongside broad contributions to pedagogy and curriculum development. He is a recipient of HKUST’s inaugural School of Science Teaching Award and the Michael G. Gale Medal for Distinguished Teaching, and serves on the Board of Directors of the iGEM Foundation and the World Economic Forum’s Global Future Council.

Afternoon Workshops

Workshop 1: Introduction to using Tencent's WorkBuddy AI platform

This hands-on workshop by instructors from the Tencent WeTech Academy introduces the WorkBuddy platform and its key features, guiding participants through its core functions, practical applications, and user workflow. Students will learn how WorkBuddy supports collaboration, task management, and productivity in everyday work settings.

Students should bring their laptops and register for a WorkBuddy account (free tokens will be provided for hackathon participants).
 
Supported by the Tencent WeTech Academy, Tencent Cloud

About the facilitator: James Bishop, Koru Consulting

James is a Learning Experience Designer from Koru Consulting who helps people and teams turn complex challenges into engaging, practical learning experiences. He has worked with all of Hong Kong’s universities, as well as institutions and organisations around the world, designing and facilitating programmes in innovation, collaboration and human-centred problem-solving.  Known for his energetic, highly participatory style, James makes powerful frameworks accessible, memorable and immediately useful.

https://www.linkedin.com/in/james-bishop-koru/

Transport

You are encouraged to take the MTR, public transport or a taxi to the Lecture Hall II. If you take the MTR, please get off at HKU Station and exit from C1, from there you can walk to the Centennial Campus. If you take a bus or minibus, you should get off at the bus stop outside Haking Wong Building on Pokfulam Road. Click here for the campus map (search for “Lee Shau Kee Lecture Centre”).

The Lecture Hall II is located on the LG level, Centennial Campus. Google Map: https://maps.app.goo.gl/DJzU2XBmoRYNMbjP7

MTR

HKU Station, use Exit C1.
Take the escalators up to the footbridge. The escalators on the other side of the bridge will take you to the Centennial Campus.

 Parking

Suggested drop off points are at Centennial Campus Car Park or at the back of the Jockey Club Tower.
The best carparks on campus for Grand Hall visitors will be the Centennial Campus Carpark (47 spaces) or the Composite Building Carpark (145 spaces). For further enquiries, please contact Security & Parking Unit at +852 3917 2882 or click here.
